Key concerns: eval parity with OpenAI, compatibility with TGI/vLLM toolchains, SSO/KMS/audit logs, and ability to run a pilot with production-like traffic.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-17 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42 minutes | Recording: yes | Meeting ID: ff-20260917-lumina-01
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Rachel Chen (Lumina CTO), Daniel Park (Lumina ML Eng), Sara Ahmed (Lumina Security)

00:00 Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining. i'm alex from redwood, ae for the lumina account, with sofia our se. quick agenda - understand your current infra, blockers for migration, security needs, and next steps for a pilot. rachel over to you to give quick context.
00:15 Rachel: yeah thanks alex, so we've been running most prod traffic through openai for chat and few-shot tasks. we're also experimenting with vllm locally for cheaper batch scoring; tgi is in our bench for model infra experiments. main driver here is cost predictability and trimming tail latency for patient-facing features. recruitment teams noticed 300-400ms variance on some flows.
00:42 Daniel: to add, our prod qps is around 20-30 at peak for chat completions, embeddings jobs run overnight. we care about embedding parity too - we use openai text-embedding-3-small currently.
00:58 Sofia: got it. are you using the openai chat API or completions for most paths? any function-calling?
01:05 Daniel: mostly chat API with some function calling. plus a few internal microservices call the completions API for template generation.
01:12 Sara: and from security, we need SOC2 in place, SAML SSO, KMS for key management, and ability to have audit logs retained for at least 1 year. also data residency concern - EU patient data should stay in eu region.
01:30 Alex: perfect, that's the typical checklist. quick callouts on Redwood: hosted API is easiest, but seems like you're pushing towards dedicated for cost predictability and throughput - does that sound right?
01:44 Rachel: yeah hosted is fine for some experiments but for production we prefer dedicated. main questions - how close will model outputs match openai? and how hard is it to migrate prompts and tooling (we use TGI/vLLM internally too).
02:02 Sofia: on parity - we often see small differences due to tokenization, sampling defaults, and model version. we do onboarding tests where we run the customer's eval suite across both endpoints and measure quality/regression. for OpenAI models we offer curated model variants and recommended sampling/temperature mappings to match behavior.
02:30 Daniel: when you say curated variants, do you mean you host the same checkpoints or reimplement behavior?
02:36 Sofia: we host open-source checkpoints and optimize runtime for throughput; for closed-source we map to closest open checkpoints and tune defaults. we also provide a small compatibility shim for prompt tokens and chat formatting - most customers hit parity within a <2-3% eval delta on intent/accuracy metrics, but we highlight edge cases.
02:58 Sara: concerning vLLM/TGI - we run some local workloads with vllm because it's cheaper but less stable at scale. will moving to Dedicated mean we have to change our orchestration?
03:10 Alex: Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool you run with Redwood-managed runtime. you can keep your orchestration for pre/post processing; integration is via our API. for teams using vllm/TGI, we usually help with migrating their inference scripts - wrappers are small, mostly around tokenization and kv cache handling.
03:30 Daniel: how about the KV cache behavior? our latency improvements depend a lot on cache hits for long-running threads.
03:38 Sofia: our runtime supports incremental KV cache and session pinning; semantics are similar to vllm's kv cache. we expose session APIs so you can re-use cached past keys - in benchmarks we've seen 20-40% token cost reduction with prefix caching for dialogue workloads.
03:58 Rachel: can you run a quick parity test? like we send 1000 prompts from our eval set and you run OpenAI vs Redwood Dedicated vs our vLLM snapshot and show latency/cost/accuracy?
04:10 Alex: absolutely. typical next step: you send the eval set and traffic profile, sofia runs parity/baseline tests and we'll share a benchmark spreadsheet. we'll also include a cost model for hosted vs dedicated.
04:22 Daniel: what about embeddings compatibility? we need vector similarity to match existing indexes - reindexing is expensive across hundreds of millions of documents.
04:32 Sofia: we support multiple embedding models; if you want to avoid reindexing we can run a sample - compute vectors from a sample corpus across both systems and measure cosine distance drift. some drift is expected; we aim to keep similarity high enough that top-k doesn't change significantly.
04:55 Sara: security: can dedicated run inside our VPC or on-prem? and what about KMS/HSM integration?
05:03 Alex: yes - Redwood Private is the VPC/on-prem option. Dedicated can be provisioned in specific cloud regions with customer-managed networking options and private peering, plus KMS integrations. for HSM-level keys we'd talk to our security team; typical customers use KMS with envelope encryption.
05:22 Sara: audit logs - we need fine-grained per-request logging and retention controls.
05:27 Sofia: we provide request-level traces and token-level cost metrics inside the console; audit log export is available to S3 or SIEM with configurable retention. retention beyond default can be enabled as an add-on.
05:42 Rachel: curious about rollback and model rollouts - we have safety/regression concerns and need canarying.
05:50 Sofia: rollouts are supported: canary, A/B, automatic fallback policies. you can pin a route to a specific model version and set thresholds for automated rollback if quality metrics drop.
06:05 Daniel: network latency concerns - our users are EU-based, so we need eu region endpoints. do you have hardware in eu-west?
06:12 Alex: yes we have dedicated capacity options in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1; we can plan the pilot in eu and ensure data doesn't egress.
06:20 Rachel: cost question - how much cheaper is dedicated vs openai per token?
06:26 Alex: it depends on committed capacity and workload profile; we provide a model that compares per-token hosted pricing vs reserved monthly commits. typical customers with sustained qps see 30-60% reduction in unit cost when moving to Dedicated plus batching/caching optimizations. we'll send a tailored estimate.
06:44 Daniel: any gotchas moving from openai's chat format? our app expects function-calling behavior and structured outputs.
06:52 Sofia: we support function calling and structured output with JSON schema enforcement; there are small differences in streaming chunks and event ordering sometimes, but our SDK normalizes them.
07:06 Sara: legal - data residency clauses, contractual SLAs, and incident response timelines - can you share a security pack?
07:14 Alex: yes we'll attach SOC2 report, ISO attestation if applicable, pen test summary, and our standard contract template. i can send those right after the call.
07:25 Rachel: timeline - we want a pilot in ~3 weeks and production in 8-12 weeks if parity checks out.
07:33 Alex: that sounds reasonable. pilot scope would be a small dedicated pool, run your eval traffic, and then increase capacity. sofia - do you want anything else to run the parity tests?
07:40 Sofia: sample prompt set, 1-2 representative long threads for kv-cache test, embeddings sample, and a small set of structured output prompts. also an indication of peak qps and average tokens per request.
07:50 Daniel: i'll package that and upload to the secure folder. is there a recommended format?
07:54 Sofia: csv/json with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output (optional), user_session_id for threads. for embeddings provide 10k sample vectors in text file.
08:10 Alex: recap of next steps - alex send pricing and security docs; sofia run parity once they send assets; schedule security deep dive. any other questions?
08:22 Rachel: no, that's it. thanks both.
08:26 Meeting end.

Notes: transcription has a few ASR substitutions (vLLM often transcribed as 'vllm' or 'v-L-M'); speaker labels mostly accurate but sometimes overlap.
